newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE'S FOREIGN DEBT RISES TO $24.4 BILLION.
newsitem.headline: CHILE'S FOREIGN DEBT RISES TO $24.4 BILLION.

text.p: Chile's foreign debt rose to $1.45 billion in the first six months of the year to total $24.43 billion on June 30, said the Central Bank in its monthly report.
Medium and long-term foreign loans came to $4.04 billion in the first half of the year with over 90 percent going to the private sector.
Chilean companies issued foreign bonds worth $750 million between January and June which represented 20 percent of the funds received by private companies, it said.
Private medium and long term debt rose to 79 percent of the total debt in June from 76 percent in 1996.
The public sector has trimmed its medium and long term debt by $45 million in the first six months of the year, while private sector debt climbed by $2.57 billion.
